topic.name: Solving Polynomial Equations Using the GCF

question.explanation:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form $P_n(x)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} 2x^3 + 14x^2 + x &= 7x^2 - 2x\\[3pt] 2x^3 + 7x^2 + x &= -2x\\[3pt] 2x^3 + 7x^2 + 3x & = 0 \end{align}

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $x.$ We can factor out the $x$ as follows: \begin{align} 2x^3 + 7x^2 + 3x & = 0\\[3pt] x(2x^2 + 7x +3) & = 0\\[3pt] \end{align}

Now, we factor the expression $2x^2 + 7x +3$ as follows: \begin{align} x(2x^2 + 7x +3) & = 0\\[3pt] x(2x + 1)(x +3) & = 0 \end{align}

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $x = 0,$ $x = -\dfrac{1}{2},$ and $x = -3.$

example.title: Solving a Cubic Equation by Rearranging

question.text: Determine the real roots of the cubic equation $2x^3-40x^2+35x=-3x^3.$
question.explanation:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form $P_n(x)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} 2x^3-40x^2+35x=-3x^3\\[3pt] 5x^3-40x^2+35x & = 0 \end{align}

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $5x.$ We can factor out the $5x$ as follows: \begin{align} 5x^3-40x^2+35x & = 0\\[3pt] 5x(x^2 -8x + 7) & = 0\\[3pt] \end{align}

Now, we factor the expression $x^2 -8x + 7$ as follows: \begin{align} 5x(x^2 -8x + 7) & = 0\\[3pt] 5x(x - 1)(x - 7) & = 0 \end{align}

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $x = 0,$ $x = 1,$ and $x = 7.$

example.title: Solving a Cubic Equation by Rearranging

question.explanation:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form $P_n(t)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} 20t^3+5t^2&=12t-3t^2\\[3pt] 20t^3+8t^2&=12t\\[3pt] 20t^3+8t^2-12t & = 0 \end{align}

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $4t.$ We can factor out the $4t$ as follows: \begin{align} 20t^3+8t^2-12t & = 0\\[3pt] 4t(5t^2 + 2t - 3) & = 0\\[3pt] \end{align}

Now, we factor the expression $5t^2 + 2t - 3$ as follows: \begin{align} 4t(5t^2 + 2t - 3) & = 0\\[3pt] 4t(5t - 3)(t + 1) & = 0 \end{align}

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $t = 0,$ $t = \dfrac{3}{5},$ and $t = -1.$
